items.title: AI掀起大型併購潮！傳邁威爾洽購Lumentum 規模有望躋身科技電信併購史前十大
items.title_en: AI Fuels Wave of Mega Mergers! Marvell Said to Be in Talks to Acquire Lumentum, Deal Could Rank Among Top Ten Tech‑Telecom Acquisitions
paras: 人工智慧(AI)產業競相擴大規模之際，彭博引述知情人士說法報導，邁威爾科技(Marvell)(MRVL-US)正與資料中心光學設備製造商Lumentum(LITE-US)進行深入洽談，考慮收購這家公司以簡化供應鏈。
這兩家總部位於北加州的公司展開洽談，凸顯AI發展正引發一波併購熱潮，投資人看好這項技術龐大的成長潛力。Lumentum目前市值約830億美元，邁威爾市值則約2,210億美元。
知情人士表示，交易最快可能於下周宣布，但由於雙方尚未達成最終協議，談判仍可能破局，交易時程等細節也可能改變。邁威爾與Lumentum的代表均未置評。
收購傳聞曝光後，邁威爾周三盤後股價下跌約9%，Lumentum則一度大漲約11%，使市值達到約910億美元。Lumentum今年股價已上漲148%，周三正常交易收盤價為每股913.95美元。
根據彭博的統計數據，這筆交易若成真，可能擠進科技與電信業史上規模前十大的併購案。
Lumentum生產雷射及其他光學技術產品，可用於高速傳輸大量資料。這類硬體是AI熱潮的重要基礎，讓資料中心及電信業者得以在伺服器、不同設施與其他目的地之間傳輸資訊。
邁威爾是一家半導體製造商，目前向Lumentum採購雷射產品，因此這筆交易可能簡化其供應鏈。邁威爾持續加碼光學與光子技術，以連接資料中心設備，今年稍早收購了光子技術公司Celestial AI。
輝達(NVDA-US)先前也投資Lumentum 20億美元，協議內容包括雙方在光子技術方面合作。光子技術利用光而非傳統銅線傳輸資料，能以更快、更有效率的方式傳送資訊。
邁威爾也與亞馬遜(AMZN-US)旗下雲端部門及微軟(MSFT-US)合作，協助兩家公司開發客製化AI晶片。邁威爾8月與Alphabet(GOOGL-US)旗下Google達成晶片協議，支援Google自行開發的AI晶片張量處理器(TPU)，協議也讓Google有權購買價值最高122億美元的邁威爾股票。
隨著客製化AI晶片及網路產品需求激增，邁威爾已成為AI支出熱潮的最大受惠者之一，今年股價幾乎上漲兩倍。邁威爾本月稍早將2028會計年度營收預測從150億美元上修至200億美元，理由是資料中心使用的客製化AI晶片及網路產品需求強勁。
不過Bernstein分析師表示，這筆潛在交易的規模可能引發市場對融資及整合問題的疑慮，並指出以如此龐大的收購規模，邁威爾可能無法完全以現金支付收購款項。截至最近一季，邁威爾的現金及約當現金約為39.2億美元。
paras_en: As the artificial‑intelligence (AI) industry races to scale up, Bloomberg reported, citing sources, that Marvell Technology (MRVL‑US) is in deep talks with data‑center optics maker Lumen­tium (LITE‑US) about a possible acquisition to simplify its supply chain.

Both companies, headquartered in Northern California, have opened negotiations, underscoring how AI development is sparking a merger frenzy that investors view as having massive growth potential. Lumen­tium’s market value is currently about $83 billion, while Marvell’s is roughly $221 billion.

Sources say the deal could be announced as early as next week, but because no final agreement has been reached, the talks could still fall apart and timing details may change. Neither Marvell nor Lumen­tium commented on the matter.

After the acquisition rumor broke, Marvell’s after‑hours share price fell about 9% on Wednesday, while Lumen­tium’s surged roughly 11%, lifting its market cap to about $91 billion. Lumen­tium’s stock is up 148% year‑to‑date, closing at $913.95 per share on Wednesday’s regular session.
Bloomberg’s data indicate that if the transaction closes, it could squeeze into the top ten largest mergers ever in the technology and telecommunications sectors.

Lumen­tium manufactures lasers and other optical‑technology products used for high‑speed, high‑volume data transmission. Such hardware is a key foundation of the AI boom, enabling data‑centers and telecom operators to move information between servers, facilities and other destinations.

Marvell, a semiconductor maker, currently buys laser products from Lumen­tium, so the deal could streamline its supply chain. Marvell is ramping up its optics and photonics capabilities to connect data‑center equipment and earlier this year acquired photonics firm Celestial AI.

Nvidia (NVDA‑US) previously invested $2 billion in Lumen­tium, with an agreement that the two would cooperate on photonics technology. Photonics uses light rather than traditional copper wiring to transmit data, allowing faster and more efficient information transfer.

Marvell also works with Amazon’s (AMZN‑US) cloud division and Microsoft (MSFT‑US) to help the two firms develop custom AI chips. In August, Marvell struck a chip deal with Google, an Alphabet (GOOGL‑US) subsidiary, to support Google’s own AI tensor‑processing units (TPUs) and gave Google the right to purchase up to $12.2 billion of Marvell stock.

With exploding demand for custom AI chips and networking gear, Marvell has become one of the biggest beneficiaries of the AI‑spending surge, its stock having nearly doubled this year. Earlier this month Marvell lifted its FY 2028 revenue outlook from $15 billion to $20 billion, citing strong demand for custom AI chips and networking products in data centers.

However, Bernstein analysts warn that the sheer size of the potential deal could raise market concerns about financing and integration, noting that a transaction of this magnitude may not be payable entirely in cash. As of the most recent quarter, Marvell’s cash and cash equivalents were about $3.92 billion.

根據《彭博》週三（28日）引述知情人士報導，雙方最快可能於下周宣布交易，但目前尚未達成最終協議，包含公布時程在內的相關細節仍可能變動。
Lumentum市值約83億美元，Marvell市值約221億美元。消息公布後，邁威爾盤後股價下跌逾8%，Lumentum則上漲11%。
隨著市場看好AI發展前景，科技業者正透過併購擴大在AI基礎設施領域的布局。Lumentum專注於雷射與光學技術，產品應用於伺服器、資料中心及其他節點之間的高速資料傳輸，是支撐AI運算基礎設施的重要硬體供應商。
隨著AI模型訓練與推論對頻寬需求持續增加，資料中心及電信業者對高速光學元件的需求也隨之提升。
今年稍早，輝達(NVDA-US) 已向Lumentum投資20億美元，凸顯其在AI供應鏈中的重要性。
分析指出，對邁威爾而言，收購Lumentum也具有供應鏈整合的戰略意義。邁威爾本身是半導體業者，目前已向Lumentum採購雷射產品。
若交易順利完成，邁威爾將可把關鍵供應商納入旗下，進一步簡化供應鏈，並深化AI資料中心光電互連領域的垂直整合。
兩家公司總部均位於加州北部。

items.title: 「中國製造」轉型！電動車、AI零組件與工業機械崛起 出口版圖改寫全球競爭
items.title_en: "Made in China" Transforms: EVs, AI Components, and Industrial Machinery Rise, Redrawing Global Export Competition
paras: 過去提到「中國製造」，外界往往聯想到低價T恤、塑膠玩具與家具，如今這個標籤正快速轉變，電動休旅車、人工智慧(AI)基礎設施零組件、高階化學品、工業機械與智慧家電，逐漸成為中國出口的新主力。《路透社》10月28日報導指出，中國透過逾10年的國家政策扶植與產業升級，持續往全球製造業價值鏈上游移動，不僅在汽車出口市場取得優勢，也開始擴大在工廠設備、工業機器人及AI相關硬體供應鏈的影響力。
中國是全球第二大經濟體，近年出口結構出現明顯變化。汽車是其中最受矚目的代表，中國對海外市場的汽車銷售規模已超越德國與美國的合計出口量。相較之下，鞋類、玩具、家具等傳統出口商品的出口表現則停滯甚至下滑。這波轉型一方面為全球消費者帶來價格相對低廉、功能與品質不斷提升的產品，另一方面也讓美國、德國等傳統製造業國家的企業面臨更激烈的競爭，部分工廠與就業機會可能因此受到衝擊。
中國製造業的擴張，與政府長期扶植及國內經濟結構密切相關。中國政府透過補貼與產業政策支持企業擴產、投入新技術，試圖在房地產市場長期低迷、民眾消費信心尚未完全恢復之際，維持經濟成長動能。然而，當部分產業的生產能力超過國內需求，企業便更加依賴海外市場消化產量，低價出口也因此成為中國製造業擴張的重要途徑，並加深與貿易夥伴之間的摩擦。
AI熱潮進一步凸顯中國在全球供應鏈中的新角色。雖然最先進的AI晶片主要由美國企業設計、在台灣製造，但建構AI資料中心所需的其他硬體，仍有相當一部分仰賴中國供應，包括成熟製程晶片、一般記憶體、伺服器零組件、變壓器、電線、電路控制板及電力設備等。這些產品未必是最受市場關注的尖端晶片，卻是AI運算基礎設施不可或缺的實體設備。
數據顯示，2026年上半年中國晶片出口金額接近翻倍，達1,772.8億美元；同期電腦與伺服器出口則年增41.3%。《路透社》引述東尼布萊爾全球變革研究所(Tony Blair Institute for Global Change)資深地緣政治顧問Ruby Osman指出，AI正在改變中國的貿易版圖，尤其是成熟製程晶片與周邊實體設備，中國再次取得領先地位。

2025年各類AI相關產品的出口數據也顯示，中國在多種電力與電子零組件的國際供應鏈中占有重要位置。相關品項包括電力變壓器、積體電路、辦公設備零組件、絕緣電線、低電壓保護設備、電氣控制板、發電機組及電力配件。依《路透社》整理的八類AI基礎設施相關產品出口趨勢，中國在其中五類已成為最大出口國。不過，這些統計品項也包含部分非AI用途產品，且中國與香港分別計算出口數據，香港數據亦包含轉口貿易，因此不能將全部出口金額直接視為AI產業營收。
化學品產業同樣反映中國由低階製造邁向高附加價值產品的趨勢。過去中國主要生產較基礎的化學品，再從歐洲、日本及美國進口高價值產品，如今則逐步擴大有機化學品、塑膠原料及多種特殊化學材料的出口，應用範圍涵蓋汽車保險桿使用的彈性塑料、太陽能板材料，以及自行車使用的碳纖維等。
根據經濟合作暨發展組織(OECD)數據，中國化學品企業過去10年累計獲得約750億美元補貼，2023年補貼金額一度達約150億美元。中國官方數據顯示，2018年至2023年間，當地新增約5,000家化學品企業。產能快速擴張也造成部分大宗化學品供過於求，部分工廠被迫閒置，生產商則將庫存推向海外市場。

包括巴斯夫(BASF) (BASFY)、陶氏(Dow) (DOW)、利安德巴塞爾(LyondellBasell) (LYB)、住友化學(Sumitomo Chemical)、英力士(INEOS)及三菱化學(Mitsubishi Chemical)等企業，過去一年均曾向投資人示警，中國競爭者在價格與生產規模上的優勢，正對其獲利構成壓力。中國化學品出口成長因此呈現兩面性：一方面代表產業技術與供應能力提升，另一方面也可能因擴產過快，加劇全球市場的價格競爭。
中國不只出口製成品，也逐漸成為供應其他國家建設工廠所需設備的重要來源。中國工業機器人出口額自2015年以來增加逾300%，持續搶占美國、德國與義大利製造商的市場；中國也已超越德國，成為全球最大的機床出口國。2025年出口數據顯示，中國機械設備出口規模已接近德國，工業機器人出口則排名全球第二，僅次於日本。
這項變化意味著，中國的競爭力不再局限於低價消費品，而是進一步延伸至製造業本身所需的生產工具。歐洲在資本財市場仍占重要地位，但其優勢正在縮小。高盛估計，歐洲在全球資本財需求量中的占比，已從2005年的54%降至43%；中國占比則從7%升至24%。德國光學設備與荷蘭半導體製造設備等高階技術仍不容易被取代，但中國正逐步擴大在各類工廠基礎設備上的供應能力。
匯豐銀行(HSBC)亞洲區首席經濟學家Fred Neumann指出，建設工廠可能需要採購中國製造的機械設備，更大的問題是，工廠後續的生產流程也可能持續依賴中國製造的零組件。這使得各國即使透過關稅限制中國商品，也未必能在短期內完全擺脫對中國供應鏈的依賴。
汽車則是中國出口轉型最具代表性的產業。中國電動車製造商不只憑藉價格優勢進入海外市場，也逐漸改變消費者對中國汽車品質與產品設計的看法。歐洲汽車製造商協會數據顯示，2026年上半年，零跑汽車(Leapmotor)在歐洲銷售的車款數量較2025年同期增加558%，比亞迪(BYD)車款銷量則成長146%。
中國汽車出口金額自2015年以來大幅攀升，2025年已成為全球第二大汽車出口國，僅次於德國。若單看中國汽車出口金額，2015年至2025年累計增幅達1,871%，且自2020年起成長明顯加快。背後原因之一是中國汽車產能快速擴張，國內市場卻難以吸收所有產量，車廠因而積極尋找海外買家。
大量價格具競爭力的中國汽車進入海外市場，也引發美國與歐洲的警戒，兩地陸續採取貿易壁壘措施，以保護本土汽車製造商。這場競爭與1980年代日本汽車出口崛起所引發的貿易摩擦有相似之處，但如今中國企業的競爭範圍已不只汽車，還涵蓋電池、電子設備、化學材料及工廠機械等多個領域。
智慧家電則是中國製造商將既有技術轉向新市場的另一個例子。中國企業正從傳統低價電子產品，擴展至掃地機器人、智慧吸塵器與機器人割草機等較高階的家用設備。由於中國本土草坪割草機市場有限，相關企業更加依賴海外需求，並逐步搶占歐美品牌的市場。
中國企業也將汽車產業累積的人工智慧、大數據與衛星定位技術，運用到其他產品上。例如，機器人割草機可使用與電動車輔助駕駛系統類似的高精度衛星定位技術，辨識草坪範圍並沿著虛擬邊界行進。這種技術轉用，讓中國企業能將原本因汽車產業快速發展而累積的能力，轉化為新的出口產品。
中國智慧家電的擴張也對美國企業造成衝擊。美國掃地機器人品牌iRobot去年12月聲請破產，該公司以Roomba系列產品聞名，後來因難以抵擋中國競爭者而陷入困境。中國家電製造商杉川機器人(Picea)曾是iRobot的供應商，後來成為其所有者，凸顯中國企業在全球家電產業的角色已從代工供應商，進一步轉向掌握品牌與市場。
歐洲則是機器人割草機的重要市場，也是中國企業積極拓展的地區。去年11月，歐盟啟動反傾銷調查，起因是當地生產商指控中國競爭者的產品價格低約40%。出口數據顯示，美國在動力割草機市場受到的衝擊尤其明顯，美國此類產品出口額從2023年的10億美元，降至2025年的2.54億美元，減少約7.46億美元；中國出口額則從2023年的13億美元增加至2025年的28億美元，超過原先的兩倍。

整體而言，「中國製造」正從以勞力密集與低價商品為主的出口模式，轉向涵蓋電動車、AI基礎設施零組件、化學品、工業機械及智慧家電的多元製造體系。中國長期產業政策、政府補貼、規模化生產及技術跨領域應用，共同推動這波轉型；但產能過剩與國內需求不足，也促使企業更積極向海外銷售。對全球市場而言，中國產品帶來更低價格與更多選擇，卻同時加劇價格壓力、貿易摩擦及傳統製造業的轉型風險。未來各國面對的挑戰，不只是如何限制低價進口，更在於如何在維持供應鏈韌性、產業競爭力與消費者利益之間取得平衡。
paras_en: In the past, "Made in China" conjured images of cheap T‑shirts, plastic toys and furniture, but that label is rapidly changing as electric SUVs, AI infrastructure components, high‑end chemicals, industrial machinery and smart home appliances become the new pillars of Chinese exports. Reuters reported on Oct. 28 that after more than a decade of state policy support and industrial upgrading, China is moving upstream in the global manufacturing value chain, gaining an edge not only in auto exports but also expanding its influence in factory equipment, industrial robots and AI‑related hardware supply chains.

China, the world’s second‑largest economy, has seen a clear shift in its export structure. Cars are the most striking example – Chinese vehicle sales abroad now exceed the combined exports of Germany and the United States. By contrast, traditional export goods such as shoes, toys and furniture have stalled or even declined. This transformation offers global consumers lower‑priced products that are increasingly functional and high‑quality, while putting firms in the United States, Germany and other traditional manufacturing nations under fiercer competition, potentially threatening some factories and jobs.

China’s manufacturing expansion is closely tied to long‑term government support and domestic economic structure. Through subsidies and industrial policies, the government encourages firms to expand capacity and adopt new technologies, aiming to sustain growth while the real‑estate market remains weak and consumer confidence has not fully recovered. When production outpaces domestic demand, firms turn to overseas markets, making low‑price exports a key growth engine and heightening frictions with trade partners.

The AI boom further highlights China’s emerging role in the global supply chain. Although the most advanced AI chips are designed by U.S. firms and fabricated in Taiwan, many other hardware items needed for AI data centers rely heavily on Chinese supply – mature‑process chips, standard memory, server components, transformers, wiring, control boards and power equipment. These are not the headline‑grabbing cutting‑edge chips, but they are essential physical assets for AI computing infrastructure.

Data show that in the first half of 2026 Chinese chip export value nearly doubled to $177.28 billion, while computer and server exports grew 41.3% year‑on‑year. Reuters quoted Ruby Osman, senior geopolitical adviser at the Tony Blair Institute for Global Change, saying AI is reshaping China’s trade map, especially for mature‑process chips and related hardware, where China has reclaimed a leading position.

Export figures for 2025 also reveal China’s important place in the international supply chain for a range of AI‑related power and electronic components, including power transformers, integrated circuits, office‑equipment parts, insulated wiring, low‑voltage protection gear, electrical control boards, generator sets and power accessories. According to Reuters, China is the top exporter in five of eight AI‑infrastructure product categories, though some items also serve non‑AI uses and Hong Kong’s re‑export data are reported separately, so total export values cannot be taken as pure AI‑industry revenue.

The chemicals sector mirrors China’s shift from low‑value manufacturing to higher‑value products. Previously, China mainly produced basic chemicals and imported high‑value chemicals from Europe, Japan and the United States. Now it is expanding exports of organic chemicals, plastic feedstocks and specialty chemicals used in flexible automotive bumpers, solar‑panel materials and carbon‑fiber bicycle frames.

OECD data show Chinese chemical firms have received roughly $75 billion in subsidies over the past decade, with subsidies peaking at about $15 billion in 2023. Official Chinese statistics indicate that between 2018 and 2023 about 5,000 new chemical enterprises were established. Rapid capacity growth has led to oversupply of some bulk chemicals, forcing plants to idle and pushing inventories onto overseas markets.

Major players such as BASF (BASFY), Dow (DOW), LyondellBasell (LYB), Sumitomo Chemical, INEOS and Mitsubishi Chemical warned investors over the past year that Chinese competitors’ price and scale advantages are squeezing their margins. Consequently, Chinese chemical export growth is double‑edged: it signals rising technological and supply capabilities, but over‑expansion can intensify global price competition.

China is not only exporting finished goods but also becoming a key source of equipment for factories abroad. Since 2015, Chinese industrial‑robot exports have risen more than 300%, eroding market share from U.S., German and Italian manufacturers; China has also overtaken Germany to become the world’s largest machine‑tool exporter. 2025 data show Chinese machinery export volume is close to Germany’s, while industrial‑robot exports rank second globally behind Japan.

This shift means China’s competitiveness is no longer confined to cheap consumer items but extends to the production tools manufacturers need. Europe still holds a strong position in capital‑goods markets, but its share is shrinking. Goldman Sachs estimates Europe’s share of global capital‑goods demand fell from 54% in 2005 to 43% today, while China’s rose from 7% to 24%. High‑end German optical gear and Dutch semiconductor‑equipment remain hard to replace, yet China is steadily expanding its supply of basic factory equipment.

HSBC’s Asian chief economist Fred Neumann notes that building a factory may require Chinese‑made machinery, but the bigger issue is that the subsequent production processes will likely continue to depend on Chinese components. This makes it difficult for countries to fully unwind their reliance on Chinese supply chains simply by imposing tariffs.

Automobiles are the most emblematic sector of China’s export transformation. Chinese EV makers are not only leveraging price advantages to enter overseas markets but also reshaping consumer perceptions of Chinese vehicle quality and design. Data from the European Automobile Manufacturers Association show that in the first half of 2026 Leapmotor’s European sales volume jumped 558% versus the same period in 2025, while BYD’s sales grew 146%.

Chinese vehicle export value has surged dramatically since 2015, making China the world’s second‑largest car exporter in 2025, behind only Germany. From 2015 to 2025, total export value rose 1,871%, with acceleration after 2020. One driver is the rapid expansion of domestic auto capacity that outstrips local demand, prompting manufacturers to seek buyers abroad.

The influx of competitively priced Chinese cars into overseas markets has triggered alarm in the United States and Europe, leading to trade‑barrier measures aimed at protecting domestic automakers. The situation resembles the trade frictions sparked by Japan’s auto export boom in the 1980s, but today Chinese firms compete across cars, batteries, electronic equipment, chemical materials and factory machinery.

Smart home appliances illustrate another way Chinese manufacturers are repurposing existing technology for new markets. Companies are moving beyond low‑cost electronics into higher‑end devices such as robot vacuums, smart vacuums and robotic lawn mowers. Because the domestic market for lawn‑mowing robots is limited, firms rely heavily on overseas demand and are gradually taking market share from European and American brands.

Chinese firms are also applying AI, big‑data and satellite‑positioning expertise gained in the auto sector to other products. For example, robotic lawn mowers use high‑precision satellite positioning similar to EV driver‑assist systems to map lawns and follow virtual boundaries. This technology transfer lets Chinese companies turn capabilities built for the auto boom into new export products.

The expansion of Chinese smart‑home appliances is hitting U.S. companies. iRobot, known for its Roomba vacuums, filed for bankruptcy in December after struggling to compete with Chinese rivals. Chinese appliance maker Picea, once an iRobot supplier, later acquired the company, highlighting a shift from contract manufacturing to owning brands and market presence.

Europe is a key market for robotic lawn mowers and a focus of Chinese expansion. In November last year the EU launched an anti‑dumping investigation after local producers accused Chinese competitors of pricing their products about 40% lower. Export data show the U.S. lawn‑mower market was hit hard, with export value falling from $1 billion in 2023 to $254 million in 2025 – a drop of roughly $746 million – while Chinese exports rose from $1.3 billion to $2.8 billion, more than doubling.

Overall, “Made in China” is shifting from a labor‑intensive, low‑price export model to a diversified manufacturing system that includes EVs, AI‑infrastructure components, chemicals, industrial machinery and smart home appliances. Long‑term industrial policies, government subsidies, scale production and cross‑sector technology applications are driving this transformation, but excess capacity and weak domestic demand also push firms to sell abroad. For global markets, Chinese products bring lower prices and greater choice, yet they also increase price pressure, trade friction and the restructuring risk for traditional manufacturers. Future challenges for countries lie not only in limiting cheap imports but also in balancing supply‑chain resilience, industrial competitiveness and consumer welfare.

items.title_en: <Earnings> Alphabet’s Revenue and Profit Disappoint, Forecasts Massive AI Spending Next Year; Shares Plunge Over 10% After Hours
paras: Alphabet(GOOGL-US)第3季營收和獲利表現都令人失望，自由現金流下滑，並預告明年度的人工智慧(AI)支出將大幅增加，最新數據加深投資人對AI投資何時帶來回報的焦慮，導致Alphabet周三(28日)盤後股價重摔逾10%。

財測關鍵數字


F2026資本支出：不變，至少2000億美元(預估區間1950-2050億美元)
F2027資本支出：大幅增加，突破3000億美元


Google第3季資本支出達513.6億美元，低於分析師預期的550.9億美元。
Alphabet維持全年資本支出預測不變。該公司第2季已將全年資本支出預估從1,900億美元上修至1,950-2,050億美元。全年資本支出預料將超過2,000億美元，2027年將進一步突破3,000億美元。
Alphabet財務長Anat Ashkenazi在財報電話會議上說：「我們仍預估2027年資本支出將大幅增加，將在第4季財報電話會議上提供更多細節。」
隨著市場對AI基礎建設支出不斷攀升的疑慮日益加深，投資人正期待公司能以可觀的投資報酬，證明大規模支出計畫的合理性。

Q3(9月30日止)財報關鍵數字 vs 分析師預期


營收：1275.8億美元 vs 1282.2億美元
調整後EPS：2.67美元 vs 3.02美元
廣告營收：820億美元 vs 836億美元
搜尋營收：633.5億美元 vs 649.6億美元
雲端營收：307億美元 vs 291億美元


Alphabet上季營收較去年同期成長25%，但這是該公司近四年來首次營收與獲利雙雙不如市場預期。反映本業的營業利益為405.8億美元，也低於分析師所估的431.9億美元。
營收不如預期，主因是Google核心廣告業務表現疲弱。
Alphabet並公布第3季自由現金流為負90.7億美元，遠低於分析師原先預期的負27億美元。這家公司以公開上市公司身分營運22年來，自由現金流在今年第2季首度轉負。
Alphabet第2季曾因持有SpaceX與Anthropic股權，獲得990.3億美元的股權投資收益，但此因素在第3季反而出現86.6億美元虧損，拖累整體獲利。

Google Cloud營收翻倍

Google持續投入大量資金推動AI業務擴張，這也帶動旗下提供各類AI服務的雲端部門營收強勁成長。
財報顯示，Google Cloud營收成長逾一倍至307億美元，超越分析師預期的287億美元，也高於原先預估的90%成長率。也Google持續從規模更大的競爭對手亞馬遜(AMZN-US)旗下AWS與微軟(MSFT-US)Azure手中搶占市占率。
Google Cloud主管Thomas Kurian首度在財報電話會議上發言，反映這個以企業客戶為主的業務部門，在傳統上以消費者業務為主的公司內部，影響力日益提升。
Kurian表示，Google張量處理器(TPU)的銷售，已成為雲端業務部門一項重要的營收來源。TPU是與輝達(NVDA-US)圖形處理器(GPU)晶片競爭的產品。
Kurian還說：「我們看到AI實驗室、資本市場、金融服務機構及企業客戶的需求都異常強勁，成長也十分可觀。」
然而，亮眼的雲端業績仍無法扭轉Google整體財報不如預期的局面。
Jefferies分析師Brent Thill說：「雲端業務是唯一超出預期的部門，成長率達103%。華爾街原本預期成長100%，因此超出幅度並不大，而且部分較高的目標也未達成。其他所有業務都不如預期。」

搜尋營收不如預期 AI模式「變現能力較低」

Alphabet搜尋業務營收成長12%至633.5億美元，低於市場預期的649.6億美元。
Google這幾年來一直努力改造搜尋引擎，以適應AI時代，試圖讓消費者繼續習慣依賴Google提供答案，因應OpenAI和Anthropic聊天機器人帶來的挑戰。如今，Google在許多搜尋結果中提供AI生成的答案，但這項轉變對過去仰賴這家搜尋巨頭帶來流量及廣告收入的企業，造成重大影響。
Google周三在電話會議上告訴分析師，AI模式的查詢已拖累搜尋相關營收的成長，該公司表示，AI模式的「變現能力較低」。
Google一直試圖運用多年來累積的用戶資訊，提供更個人化的問題答覆，以在AI競賽中建立優勢。然而近幾個月來，Google在開發AI程式編碼工具方面落後Anthropic及OpenAI，近期推出的Gemini 4宣稱該模型在程式編碼及網路安全等領域表現出色，但部分員工仍擔心尚未完全追上競爭對手。
Google周三稍早搶先公布新款Gemini 4 Carbon模型，Alphabet執行長皮查伊(Sundar Pichai)在電話會議上告訴分析師：「我們很快還會推出更多模型，包括效率更高的版本，協助開發者在速度與成本之間取得最佳平衡，並將模型部署給數十億名用戶。」
paras_en: Alphabet (GOOGL-US) posted a disappointing third‑quarter revenue and profit, with free cash flow falling, and warned that AI spending next year will rise sharply. The latest data deepened investors’ anxiety about when AI investments will pay off, sending Alphabet’s after‑hours stock down more than 10% on Wednesday (the 28th).

Key financial outlook figures

FY2026 capital expenditures: unchanged, at least $200 billion (forecast range $195‑$205 billion)
FY2027 capital expenditures: a large increase, breaking $300 billion

Google’s Q3 capital spend was $51.36 billion, below analysts’ expectation of $55.09 billion.

Alphabet keeps its full‑year cap‑ex forecast unchanged. The company had already raised its full‑year cap‑ex estimate in Q2 from $190 billion to $195‑$205 billion. Full‑year cap‑ex is now expected to exceed $200 billion, with 2027 spending pushing past $300 billion.
Alphabet CFO Anat Ashkenazi said on the earnings call, “We still expect a substantial increase in 2027 capital expenditures and will provide more detail at the Q4 earnings call.”
As concerns grow over rising AI infrastructure spending, investors are looking for the company to demonstrate a solid return on investment to justify the massive outlay.

Q3 (ended September 30) key numbers vs. analyst expectations

Revenue: $127.58 billion vs. $128.22 billion
Adjusted EPS: $2.67 vs. $3.02
Advertising revenue: $82.0 billion vs. $83.6 billion
Search revenue: $63.35 billion vs. $64.96 billion
Cloud revenue: $30.7 billion vs. $29.1 billion

Alphabet’s revenue grew 25% year‑over‑year, but this was the first time in four years that both revenue and profit missed market forecasts. Operating income from core businesses was $40.58 billion, also below analysts’ estimate of $43.19 billion.
The revenue miss was driven primarily by weak performance in Google’s core advertising business.

Alphabet reported Q3 free cash flow of negative $9.07 billion, far worse than analysts’ expectation of negative $2.7 billion. This marks the first quarterly negative free cash flow since the company went public 22 years ago, occurring in Q2 of this year.
In Q2, Alphabet booked $99.03 billion of equity‑investment gains from its stakes in SpaceX and Anthropic, but in Q3 those holdings generated a loss of $8.66 billion, dragging down overall profit.

Google Cloud revenue doubles

Google continues to pour money into expanding its AI business, which is driving strong growth in its cloud division that offers a range of AI services.

The earnings release shows Google Cloud revenue more than doubled to $30.7 billion, beating analysts’ forecast of $28.7 billion and surpassing the previously expected 90% growth rate. Google is also gaining market share from larger rivals Amazon’s AWS and Microsoft’s Azure.

Google Cloud head Thomas Kurian spoke for the first time on the earnings call, indicating that this enterprise‑focused unit is gaining influence within a company traditionally centered on consumer products.
Kurian said Google’s Tensor Processing Unit (TPU) sales have become an important revenue source for the cloud business. TPUs compete with Nvidia’s (NVDA-US) graphics processing units (GPUs).
Kurian added, “We are seeing unusually strong demand from AI labs, capital markets, financial services firms and corporate customers, and growth is very robust.”
Nevertheless, the impressive cloud performance could not offset the overall earnings shortfall.

Jefferies analyst Brent Thill commented, “Cloud is the only segment that beat expectations, growing at 103%. Wall Street originally expected 100% growth, so the outperformance is modest and some of the higher targets were missed. All other businesses fell short of expectations.”

Search revenue missed expectations; AI mode “monetization is weaker”
Alphabet’s search revenue grew 12% to $63.35 billion, below the market forecast of $64.96 billion.

Google has been over the past few years re‑engineering its search engine for the AI era, trying to keep users reliant on Google for answers in the face of challenges from OpenAI and Anthropic chatbots. Today, Google provides AI‑generated answers in many search results, a shift that has significantly impacted companies that previously depended on Google’s traffic and ad revenue.
During Wednesday’s call, Google told analysts that AI‑driven queries have weighed on search‑related revenue growth, stating that the AI mode has “lower monetization capability.”

Google has long tried to leverage its accumulated user data to deliver more personalized answers and gain an edge in the AI race. However, in recent months the company has fallen behind Anthropic and OpenAI in developing AI coding tools. Its newly launched Gemini 4 claims strong performance in coding and cybersecurity, but some employees remain concerned that it has not fully caught up with rivals.

Earlier on Wednesday, Google pre‑announced the new Gemini 4 Carbon model. Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai told analysts, “We will soon roll out more models, including more efficient versions, to help developers strike the best balance between speed and cost, and we will deploy the models to billions of users.”

items.title: Anthropic該在IPO第一天買進？散戶投資人點出關鍵
items.title_en: Should You Buy Anthropic on IPO Day? Retail Investors Highlight Key Points
paras: 人工智慧（AI）新創公司 Anthropic 即將迎來備受矚目的首次公開發行（IPO），但散戶投資人對於是否應在掛牌首日進場，仍抱持不同看法。隨著公司首度透過招股文件揭露財務狀況，投資人一方面看好其營收成長與 AI 產業前景，另一方面也對高昂算力支出、長期合約承諾及市場估值感到憂慮。
根據《Business Insider》報導，與今年夏季備受關注的 SpaceX IPO 不同，截至 Anthropic 提交的 S-1 招股文件，尚未規劃專門保留給散戶的股票配額。
SpaceX 當時則預留 20% 的股份供散戶認購，兩者的安排差異，也可能影響一般投資人的參與意願。
近期 AI 類股走勢劇烈震盪，市場對 AI 產業的看法反覆轉變，也讓 Anthropic IPO 的投資策略更難拿捏。部分投資人打算趁掛牌初期搶進，另一些人則希望等公司財務狀況與營運前景更加明朗後，再決定是否投資。

有人準備砸5萬美元進場：趁熱度獲利後快速退場

常駐阿拉伯聯合大公國的顧問兼投資人 Walid Diab 計畫投入約 3 萬至 5 萬美元買進 Anthropic 股票。
他預期，追蹤那斯達克等指數的被動型基金可能在公司上市後買進股票，帶動股價進一步上漲，因此希望把握初期買盤帶來的機會。
不過，Diab 並不打算長期持有。他曾以類似策略參與 SpaceX IPO，這次也準備在市場熱度消退前逐步退出，預計出售超過 70% 的持股。
Diab 認為，Anthropic 並不適合作為長期投資對象，因為Anthropic 選擇此時上市，可能是經過計算的時機布局。
他指出，若美國期中選舉改變華府的權力分布，AI 業者明年可能面臨更大的監管阻力，企業趁目前的市場環境上市，或許有其考量。
此外，Anthropic 的算力與基礎設施成本高昂，也可能受到伊朗戰爭引發的能源通膨影響。公司表示，2026 年上半年相關支出約達 90 億美元，並在招股文件中提醒，能源成本居高不下可能衝擊財務表現。
儘管市場估計 Anthropic 的潛在可服務市場規模超過 30 兆美元，Diab 仍認為，這項預估可能過於樂觀。
他強調，自己的策略是短期擇機進場、長期持續觀察，一旦股價估值與基本面出現明顯落差，就會迅速出場，可能會賣掉手中超過 70% 的 Anthropic 股份。

長期算力承諾逾8,000億美元　投資人擔憂財務壓力

並非所有看好 Anthropic 的投資人都願意參與 IPO。南非交易員兼財富管理人士 Raj Dass 表示，儘管 Anthropic 的營收表現出色，且看似具備相當的競爭壁壘，他仍打算避開此次 IPO。
Dass 的主要疑慮在於公司的長期算力承諾。根據 S-1 招股文件，Anthropic 的算力合約承諾金額超過 8,000 億美元。公司也提醒投資人，多年期合約可能在短期內對財務表現造成壓力，營業利潤率與營收成長都可能出現波動。
Dass 另指出，Anthropic 約有一半營收來自雲端合作夥伴，相關合作協議也可能成為潛在風險來源。他認為，目前要判斷 Anthropic 的競爭優勢能否持續，以及未來商業模式是否具備足夠韌性，仍言之過早。
市場對 AI 產業的情緒變化，同樣加深投資人的不確定性。過去幾個月，投資人一度擔心 AI 可能威脅人類，也曾因 AI 代理技術的發展而轉趨樂觀，近期又重新關注 AI 是否可能對金融市場與整體經濟構成系統性風險。
預測市場 Polymarket 上，投資人對 Anthropic 的未來也呈現兩極看法。市場除了押注公司將快速成長，也有人押注其最終可能走向失敗；相關市場甚至反映，Anthropic 在本世紀結束前宣告破產的機率約為 21%。

仍有投資人看好AI長期發展　不因短期股價下跌退場

相較於採取短線策略的 Diab，以及決定暫時觀望的 Dass，英國散戶投資人 Prashant Mishra 則打算長期持有 Anthropic 股票。
Mishra 表示，他與妻子都計畫向券商提出 IPO 認購申請，若獲准參與，兩人各自至少投入 1,000 美元，並預計持有數年。
他相信 AI 具有改變產業的潛力，即使 Anthropic 上市後股價迅速下跌，也不至於因此被迫賣出。他引用投資圈廣為流傳、歸於股神巴菲特的說法，強調只要尚未賣出，就不能算真正虧損。
不過，Mishra 也注意到 Anthropic 面臨的經營挑戰，包括借貸成本上升，以及公司與輝達(NVDA-US) 之間緊密交織的 AI 交易關係。部分市場專業人士擔憂，若這類交易網絡中的某個環節出現問題，風險可能進一步擴散。
對 Mishra 而言，關鍵在於龐大的資料中心投資能否逐步降低成本。他認為，若 Anthropic 無法透過這些投資創造足夠的經濟價值，股價終究可能面臨崩跌風險。
paras_en: Artificial intelligence (AI) startup Anthropic is about to launch a highly anticipated initial public offering (IPO), but retail investors remain divided on whether to enter on the first day of trading. As the company discloses its financials for the first time in its prospectus, investors are optimistic about revenue growth and the AI industry's outlook, yet they are also concerned about hefty compute costs, long‑term contract commitments, and market valuation.
According to Business Insider, unlike the much‑watched SpaceX IPO this summer, Anthropic’s S‑1 filing shows no dedicated share allocation for retail investors.
SpaceX had set aside 20% of its shares for retail subscription, and the difference in allocation could affect ordinary investors’ willingness to participate.

AI‑related stocks have been extremely volatile lately, and shifting market sentiment on the AI sector makes the Anthropic IPO strategy even harder to pin down. Some investors plan to jump in early, while others prefer to wait until the company’s financials and operating outlook are clearer before deciding to invest.

One person is ready to throw $50,000 into the deal, aiming to profit from the hype and exit quickly. Walid Diab, a consultant and investor based in the United Arab Emirates, plans to invest roughly $30,000‑$50,000 in Anthropic shares.
He expects passive funds that track indices such as the Nasdaq to buy the stock after the listing, pushing the price higher, and wants to capture that early buying pressure.

However, Diab does not intend to hold long‑term. He used a similar approach for the SpaceX IPO and this time plans to unwind his position before the hype fades, targeting the sale of more than 70% of his holdings.
Diab argues that Anthropic is not a suitable long‑term investment because its decision to go public now may be a calculated timing play.

He notes that if the U.S. midterm elections shift power in Washington, AI firms could face tougher regulation next year, and companies may be taking advantage of the current market environment to list.

In addition, Anthropic’s compute and infrastructure costs are massive and could be hit by energy‑price inflation sparked by the Iran war. The company says it expects roughly $9 billion in related expenses in the first half of 2026 and warns that persistently high energy costs could hurt its financial performance.
Even though the market estimates Anthropic’s addressable market at over $30 trillion, Diab believes that figure is overly optimistic.

He stresses his strategy is short‑term opportunistic entry with ongoing monitoring, and he will exit quickly once the stock’s valuation diverges sharply from fundamentals, potentially selling more than 70% of his Anthropic shares.

Not all investors who are bullish on Anthropic want to join the IPO. South African trader and wealth manager Raj Dass says that despite strong revenue performance and apparent competitive moats, he plans to stay away from this offering.

Dass’s main concern is the company’s long‑term compute commitments. The S‑1 reveals Anthropic has pledged compute contracts exceeding $800 billion, and the firm warns that multi‑year contracts could pressure short‑term financial results, causing volatility in operating margins and revenue growth.

He also points out that roughly half of Anthropic’s revenue comes from cloud partners, and those agreements could become a source of risk. He believes it is still too early to judge whether Anthropic’s competitive advantage will endure or if its business model has sufficient resilience.

Shifts in sentiment toward the AI sector also deepen investor uncertainty. In recent months, investors have swung from fearing AI could threaten humanity, to optimism about AI agents, and now back to concerns that AI might pose systemic risks to financial markets and the broader economy.

On the prediction market Polymarket, investors hold polarized views on Anthropic’s future. Some bet on rapid growth, while others wager the company could ultimately fail; the market even reflects a roughly 21% perceived probability that Anthropic will go bankrupt before the end of the century.

Other investors remain optimistic about AI’s long‑term prospects and are not deterred by short‑term price drops. Compared with Diab’s short‑term play and Dass’s wait‑and‑see stance, UK retail investor Prashant Mishra intends to hold Anthropic stock for the long haul.
Mishra says he and his wife plan to submit an IPO subscription request through their broker, and if approved each will invest at least $1,000 and hold the shares for several years.

He believes AI has the power to transform industries, and even if Anthropic’s price falls sharply after the listing, they would not be forced to sell. He cites a widely shared Buffett‑attributed saying that a position isn’t a real loss until it’s sold.

Mishra also notes Anthropic faces operational challenges, including rising borrowing costs and a tightly intertwined AI trading relationship with Nvidia (NVDA‑US). Some market professionals worry that a problem in any part of that network could amplify risk.

For Mishra, the key is whether massive data‑center investments can gradually lower costs. He thinks that if Anthropic cannot generate enough economic value from those investments, the stock could eventually face a collapse risk.

items.title: 川普認定進口機器人威脅國安！暫不加徵關稅 180天內展開談判
items.title_en: Trump Deems Imported Robots a National Security Threat, Delays Tariffs and Calls for 180-Day Negotiations
paras: 美國總統川普周三 (28日) 認定，進口機器人及工業機械對美國國家安全構成風險，但暫時未立即加徵關稅，而是指示美國商務部與美國貿易代表署和各國貿易夥伴展開談判，處理相關產品的進口問題。川普要求相關部門在180天內回報談判進展，並保留日後視談判結果採取關稅等進一步措施的權利。
這項決定暫時讓仰賴海外供應的美國製造商免於立即承受新增關稅，但也意味著機器人及工業機械供應鏈仍面臨政策不確定性。美國商務部指出，美國目前對多數類型的機器人及工業機械仰賴外國進口，國內產能不足以滿足持續增加的需求。川普政府認為，這種依賴可能對美國國防、關鍵基礎設施及製造業競爭力構成威脅。
川普是在歷經一年多的調查後作出上述決定。美國政府於2025年9月啟動調查，檢視進口機器人、工業機械及相關產品對國家安全的影響。調查範圍涵蓋可程式控制的機械系統、工業沖壓與壓製設備，以及用於切削、焊接和搬運工件的機床，另包括高壓滅菌設備、工業烤箱、雷射切割設備及水刀切割機械等。
白宮周三公布的政策文件指出，川普依據《1962年貿易擴張法》第232條採取行動，認定相關進口產品可能損害美國國家安全。根據該項決定，美國商務部長與美國貿易代表須共同和各國談判，尋求處理機器人、工業機械及其零組件進口所帶來的安全疑慮。商務部也須持續監控進口情況，若發現有必要進一步採取措施，可向總統提出建議。
白宮表示，機器人與工業機械廣泛應用於現代製造業，包括國防、商業生產及軍民兩用領域，幾乎所有現代國防系統及關鍵基礎設施都需要相關設備。美國雖然近年增加製造業投資，但機器人及工業設備的國內產量仍低於消費需求，無法完全滿足市場需要，因此必須仰賴進口。川普政府認為，若無法建立更完整的本土機器人與工業機械產業體系，美國將持續面臨供應鏈依賴問題，並可能削弱相關產業的長期競爭力。
川普此次選擇先談判、暫不立即加徵關稅，也反映美國在強化供應鏈安全與維持製造業生產成本之間面臨的取捨。由於美國本土供應能力尚不足以滿足多數機器人與工業機械需求，若立即對進口設備課稅，可能提高美國企業採購機械、建置產線及擴充產能的成本，進而影響川普政府推動製造業回流的政策目標。
不過，暫緩關稅並不代表相關貿易風險已經解除。川普表示，未來仍可能根據談判進度及結果考慮其他措施。這代表美國政府仍保留運用關稅或其他進口調整手段的空間，外國供應商及美國製造商都必須持續關注後續政策變化。
美國對中國機器人產品的限制也已經先行推進。美國聯邦通信委員會 (FCC) 於2026年7月禁止進口新型中國機器人及電力逆變器，但相關規定仍允許既有型號的人形機器人與四足機器人進口。電力逆變器則是連接再生能源、電池、電網及資料中心設備的重要裝置。
FCC當時指出，機器人可能蒐集大量資料，若遭惡意行為者利用，可能被用於監視美國民眾、強化外國情報機構的能力，或遭遠端操控。隨著搭載人工智慧的機器人逐步進入消費市場與工業生產領域，美國政府對設備資料安全、遠端控制及供應鏈風險的關注也持續升高。
除了機器人及工業機械，美國政府近期也持續透過國家安全調查檢視其他進口產品。美國商務部於2026年7月完成對進口民用飛機、噴射發動機及相關零組件的調查，同樣認定外國產品涉及美國國家安全疑慮，顯示川普政府持續運用第232條檢視不同產業的進口依賴程度。
白宮表示，川普自重返白宮後，持續運用第232條保護美國製造業及關鍵產業，相關措施涵蓋鋼鐵、鋁、銅、汽車、卡車、木材、半導體、藥品、多晶矽及無人機等產品。政府主張，透過與貿易夥伴談判並策略性運用關稅，有助吸引私人及外國資金投入美國製造業、創造本土就業機會，並分散全球供應鏈風險。
接下來180天的談判結果，將成為美國是否進一步限制機器人與工業機械進口的重要觀察指標。若談判未能達成美國政府要求，川普仍可能考慮加徵關稅或採取其他措施；若各方能在供應鏈安全與市場需求之間取得共識，則有機會避免立即增加製造業成本。對美國製造商而言，短期內雖暫時免於新增關稅，但長期採購成本、設備供應及跨國供應鏈安排仍存在不確定性。
paras_en: U.S. President Donald Trump on Wednesday (the 28th) declared that imported robots and industrial machinery pose a risk to U.S. national security, but he did not immediately impose tariffs. Instead, he instructed the Commerce Department, the Office of the U.S. Trade Representative and foreign trade partners to begin negotiations to address the import issue, and he ordered a progress report within 180 days while reserving the right to take further actions such as tariffs based on the outcome.

The decision temporarily spares U.S. manufacturers that rely on overseas supply from an immediate tariff increase, but it also means the robot and industrial‑machinery supply chain still faces policy uncertainty. The Commerce Department noted that the United States currently depends on foreign imports for most types of robots and industrial equipment, as domestic capacity cannot meet the growing demand. The Trump administration argues that this reliance could threaten U.S. defense, critical infrastructure and manufacturing competitiveness.

Trump made the decision after more than a year of investigation. The government launched the probe in September 2025 to examine how imported robots, industrial machinery and related products affect national security. The review covered programmable mechanical systems, industrial stamping and pressing equipment, as well as machine tools used for cutting, welding and material handling, plus high‑pressure sterilization gear, industrial ovens, laser‑cutting devices and water‑jet cutters.

The White House released a policy memo on Wednesday stating that Trump is acting under Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962, deeming the relevant imports potentially harmful to U.S. national security. Under that determination, the Commerce Secretary and the U.S. Trade Representative must jointly negotiate with other nations to address safety concerns tied to robots, industrial machinery and their components. The Commerce Department must also continue monitoring imports and can advise the President on further steps if needed.

The administration noted that robots and industrial machinery are widely used in modern manufacturing, including defense, commercial production and dual‑use sectors, and that virtually every modern defense system and critical infrastructure relies on such equipment. Although U.S. manufacturing investment has risen in recent years, domestic output of robots and industrial gear remains below consumption demand, forcing reliance on imports. The Trump administration believes that without a more complete domestic robot and industrial‑machinery industry, the United States will continue to face supply‑chain dependence that could erode long‑term competitiveness.

Trump’s choice to negotiate first and hold off on immediate tariffs reflects the trade‑off between strengthening supply‑chain security and keeping manufacturing costs low. Because domestic capacity is still insufficient to meet most robot and industrial‑machinery needs, an instant tariff could raise the cost for U.S. firms buying equipment, building production lines and expanding capacity, thereby undermining the administration’s goal of reshoring manufacturing.

However, the tariff delay does not mean the trade risk has been eliminated. Trump said future measures could still be considered depending on negotiation progress and outcomes. This signals that the U.S. government retains the option to use tariffs or other import‑adjustment tools, and foreign suppliers and U.S. manufacturers must keep watching policy developments.

Restrictions on Chinese robot products have already moved forward. The Federal Communications Commission (FCC) banned the import of new Chinese robots and power inverters in July 2026, while still allowing existing models of humanoid and quadruped robots to be imported. Power inverters are key devices that connect renewable energy, batteries, grids and data‑center equipment.

The FCC warned that robots can collect large amounts of data that, if exploited by malicious actors, could be used to surveil U.S. citizens, enhance foreign intelligence capabilities, or be remotely hijacked. As AI‑enabled robots increasingly enter consumer markets and industrial production, the U.S. government’s concern over data security, remote control and supply‑chain risk continues to rise.

Beyond robots and industrial machinery, the U.S. government has recently continued national‑security reviews of other imports. In July 2026 the Commerce Department completed a review of imported civilian aircraft, jet engines and related parts, also finding foreign products to pose national‑security concerns, showing the Trump administration’s ongoing use of Section 232 to assess import dependence across sectors.

The White House said that since returning to the White House, Trump has consistently used Section 232 to protect U.S. manufacturing and critical industries, covering steel, aluminum, copper, automobiles, trucks, lumber, semiconductors, pharmaceuticals, polysilicon and drones. The administration argues that negotiating with trade partners and strategically applying tariffs helps attract private and foreign investment into U.S. manufacturing, creates domestic jobs and diversifies global supply‑chain risk.

The outcome of the 180‑day negotiations will be a key indicator of whether the United States will impose further limits on robot and industrial‑machinery imports. If talks fail to meet U.S. demands, Trump may still consider tariffs or other actions; if parties reach a consensus on supply‑chain security and market needs, immediate cost increases for manufacturers could be avoided. For U.S. manufacturers, the short‑term relief from new tariffs is temporary, while long‑term procurement costs, equipment supply and cross‑border supply‑chain arrangements remain uncertain.

items.title: SK海力士ADR狂飆13%！營益率衝破天花板達80% 看好記憶體缺貨至2030年
items.title_en: SK Hynix ADR Soars 13% as Operating Margin Hits 80% Ceiling, Memory Shortage Expected Through 2030
paras: 《Marketwatch》報導，SK 海力士 (SK hynix)(000660-KR) 週三 (28 日) 公布第三季財報，營收與獲利大幅成長，營業利益率更攀上 80% 的歷史新高。不過，比亮眼財報更受市場矚目的，是公司預期 AI 基礎建設投資將持續擴張，記憶體供應吃緊的局面恐延續至 2030 年。
在財報與樂觀展望激勵下，在首爾交易時段，SK 海力士週三飆漲近 11%，美股交易時段，SK 海力士ADR (SKHY-US) 狂飆13.30%，同業美光 (MU-US) 大漲超 5.8%。
SK 海力士第三季營收達 104.62 兆韓元，增至去年同期的四倍以上，較華爾街預期高出約 7%；獲利達 39.78 兆韓元，約合 297 億美元，增至去年同期的三倍以上。
第三季營業利益率較前季提高 3 個百分點至 80%，優於市場預估的 78.4%，並創下公司新高，主要受惠於記憶體價格大漲，以及高階產品銷售增加。
公司表示，第三季 DRAM 平均售價較前季上漲近三成，NAND 平均售價則上漲約兩成半。
SK 海力士在財報中指出，AI 正形成一個良性循環：生產力提升與新營收來源帶動更多 AI 應用，進一步推升基礎建設需求。隨著企業與國家層級的 AI 計畫擴大，相關投資仍有成長空間。
此外，自駕車與機器人等實體 AI 應用，也將帶動記憶體需求。不過，先進製程的技術難度，加上新生產設施建置時間漫長，將持續限制供給擴張。
為提高營運能見度，SK 海力士與其他記憶體業者一樣，正透過長期合約鎖定較高的記憶體價格。公司透露，2027 年與 2028 年的產量，均已有超過五成納入長約。
Cantor 分析師 C.J. Muse 認為，這是一份穩健的財報，但真正牽動股價的是管理層對未來的強勁展望。他指出，公司高度看好 AI 基礎建設支出的延續性，支持記憶體市場的結構性供需失衡持續至 2030 年。
然而，記憶體產業過去曾多次因擴產過度而陷入供過於求，這仍是市場對本輪景氣循環的主要疑慮。
對此，SK 海力士主管在法說會上表示，即使公司持續興建晶圓廠，高頻寬記憶體 (HBM) 等高效能產品占比上升，也需要投入更多生產資源。
Muse 則認為，本輪 AI 週期將更持久，毛利率可望維持高檔，而設備交期拉長至一至兩年，也將限制新增產能的速度。
股東回饋方面，SK 海力士預計今年執行約 100 兆韓元的回饋計畫，包括至少 30 兆韓元股利，以及至少 60 兆韓元庫藏股買回，其中已有 40 兆韓元的買回作業完成。
paras_en: MarketWatch reported that SK Hynix (SK hynix)(000660-KR) released its third‑quarter earnings on Wednesday (the 28th), showing a sharp rise in revenue and profit, with operating margin climbing to a historic high of 80%. More than the impressive results, the market is focused on the company’s outlook that AI infrastructure investment will keep expanding, potentially keeping memory supply tight until 2030.

Fueled by the earnings beat and optimistic outlook, SK Hynix surged nearly 11% during Seoul trading on Wednesday, and its ADR (SKHY‑US) jumped 13.30% in U.S. trading, while peer Micron (MU‑US) rose more than 5.8%.

SK Hynix posted third‑quarter revenue of 104.62 trillion won, more than four times the same period last year and about 7% above Wall Street forecasts; profit reached 39.78 trillion won, roughly $29.7 billion, more than three times the year‑ago figure.

The quarter’s operating margin rose three percentage points from the prior quarter to 80%, beating the market estimate of 78.4% and setting a new company record, driven mainly by a surge in memory prices and higher sales of premium products.
The company said average DRAM selling prices in the third quarter were up nearly 30% from the prior quarter, while average NAND prices rose about 25%.

SK Hynix noted in its report that AI is creating a virtuous cycle: productivity gains and new revenue streams spur more AI applications, which in turn boost infrastructure demand. As corporate and national AI programs expand, related investment still has room to grow.

In addition, physical AI applications such as autonomous vehicles and robotics will drive memory demand. However, the technical difficulty of advanced processes and the long lead time for new production facilities will continue to limit supply expansion.

To improve operational visibility, SK Hynix, like other memory makers, is locking in higher memory prices through long‑term contracts. The company disclosed that more than half of its 2027 and 2028 production volumes are already covered by such contracts.

Cantor analyst C.J. Muse said the results are solid, but what really moves the stock is management’s strong forward outlook. He highlighted the company’s confidence in sustained AI infrastructure spending, supporting a structural memory supply‑demand imbalance through 2030.
Nevertheless, the memory industry has repeatedly suffered oversupply from over‑expansion in the past, which remains the main market concern for this cycle.

In response, an SK Hynix executive told investors that even as the firm continues building fabs and the share of high‑bandwidth memory (HBM) and other high‑performance products rises, more production resources will be required.
Muse added that this AI cycle is likely to be longer, allowing margins to stay elevated, while equipment lead times of one to two years will curb the speed of new capacity additions.

Regarding shareholder returns, SK Hynix plans to execute roughly 100 trillion won of buy‑backs and dividends this year, including at least 30 trillion won in dividends and at least 60 trillion won in share repurchases, with about 40 trillion won of repurchases already completed.

台股盤前要聞 

1.中央銀行總裁楊金龍28日赴立院財委會備詢，立委提及台股交投集中於特定產業，外資調節高科技股的水位就會造成新台幣的貶值壓力。對此，楊金龍回應，央行依循「柳樹理論」讓匯率適度擺動，不會睡不安穩，並再次強調沒有楊金龍防線。
2.晶圓代工廠聯電(2303-TW)28日召開線上法說會，並宣布董事會已核准追加約32億美元資本支出，加速新加坡與台南廠區擴充工程，聯電定調在矽光子與先進封裝帶動下，未來三年內AI相關營收將從目前約3億美元大幅拉升，占全公司營收比重衝上25%。
3.半導體測試介面廠中華精測(6510-TW)28日召開線上法說會，受惠全球AI與高效能運算高階晶片測試需求強勁，第三季合併營收與獲利同步改寫歷史新高紀錄。總經理黃水可表示，看好今年全年營收年成長50%，明年也將持續維持高成長動能。
4.三五族砷化鎵PA廠穩懋(3105-TW)28日下午舉辦法說會，穩懋表示，隨著第三代衛星規格(V3)開始啟動，加上衛星直接連接手機等實際應用持續發展，目前穩懋在低軌衛星、航太及點對點傳輸通訊上等基礎建設營收已超過40%，其中光學、基礎建設營收占比第3季已過半。隨著光通訊發展持續強勁，穩懋對2027年相關非手機產品需求維持正向樂觀看法。
5.CCL(銅箔基板)股王台光電(2383-TW)在積極擴充產能且市場需求殷切推升之下，2026年第三季營收及獲利同步登頂，單季賺4個股本，稅後純益145億元，同創單季新高，相較第二季成長46.9%，相較去年同期成長265.8%。每股盈餘40.47元，累計2026年前三季稅後純益297.13億元，每股純益達82.92元。

paras_en: 1. Central Bank Governor Yang Jin‑long appeared before the Legislative Yuan’s Finance Committee on the 28th. Legislators noted that trading in Taiwan stocks is concentrated in certain sectors, and that foreign investors adjusting the level of high‑tech stocks could put downward pressure on the New Taiwan dollar. Governor Yang responded that the central bank follows the “Willow Tree Theory” to allow the exchange rate to swing moderately without causing instability, and again emphasized that there is no “Yang Jin‑long defense line.”

2. Wafer‑fab foundry United Microelectronics Corp (UMC, 2303‑TW) held an online earnings briefing on the 28th and announced that its board has approved an additional capital expenditure of about US$3.2 billion to accelerate expansion projects at its Singapore and Tainan sites. UMC projects that, driven by silicon photonics and advanced packaging, AI‑related revenue will surge from roughly US$300 million today to represent 25% of total company revenue within three years.

3. Semiconductor test‑interface company China Precision Test (6510‑TW) held an online earnings briefing on the 28th. Benefiting from strong global demand for AI and high‑performance computing chip testing, its combined Q3 revenue and profit both set new historical highs. General Manager Huang Shui‑ke said the company expects a 50% year‑over‑year revenue growth for the full year and will maintain high growth momentum into next year.

4. Gallium arsenide PA manufacturer Unimicron (3105‑TW) hosted a briefing on the afternoon of the 28th. Unimicron noted that with the launch of third‑generation satellite specifications (V3) and the continued development of direct satellite‑to‑mobile applications, its revenue from low‑earth‑orbit satellites, aerospace, and point‑to‑point communications infrastructure now exceeds 40% of total revenue, with optical and infrastructure segments accounting for more than half of Q3 revenue. The company remains optimistic about demand for non‑mobile products related to 2027 satellite and aerospace markets.

5. CCL (copper‑clad laminate) market leader Tai‑Guang Electronics (2383‑TW) saw both revenue and profit hit record highs in Q3 2026 amid aggressive capacity expansion and strong market demand. The company earned NT$145 billion after tax in the quarter—four times its equity per share—setting a new quarterly profit peak, up 46.9% from Q2 and 265.8% year‑over‑year. items.title_en: AI Fuels Wave of Mega Mergers! Marvell Said to Be in Talks to Acquire Lumentum, Deal Could Rank Among Top Ten Tech‑Telecom Acquisitions
paras: 人工智慧(AI)產業競相擴大規模之際，彭博引述知情人士說法報導，邁威爾科技(Marvell)(MRVL-US)正與資料中心光學設備製造商Lumentum(LITE-US)進行深入洽談，考慮收購這家公司以簡化供應鏈。
這兩家總部位於北加州的公司展開洽談，凸顯AI發展正引發一波併購熱潮，投資人看好這項技術龐大的成長潛力。Lumentum目前市值約830億美元，邁威爾市值則約2,210億美元。
知情人士表示，交易最快可能於下周宣布，但由於雙方尚未達成最終協議，談判仍可能破局，交易時程等細節也可能改變。邁威爾與Lumentum的代表均未置評。
收購傳聞曝光後，邁威爾周三盤後股價下跌約9%，Lumentum則一度大漲約11%，使市值達到約910億美元。Lumentum今年股價已上漲148%，周三正常交易收盤價為每股913.95美元。
根據彭博的統計數據，這筆交易若成真，可能擠進科技與電信業史上規模前十大的併購案。
Lumentum生產雷射及其他光學技術產品，可用於高速傳輸大量資料。這類硬體是AI熱潮的重要基礎，讓資料中心及電信業者得以在伺服器、不同設施與其他目的地之間傳輸資訊。
邁威爾是一家半導體製造商，目前向Lumentum採購雷射產品，因此這筆交易可能簡化其供應鏈。邁威爾持續加碼光學與光子技術，以連接資料中心設備，今年稍早收購了光子技術公司Celestial AI。
輝達(NVDA-US)先前也投資Lumentum 20億美元，協議內容包括雙方在光子技術方面合作。光子技術利用光而非傳統銅線傳輸資料，能以更快、更有效率的方式傳送資訊。
邁威爾也與亞馬遜(AMZN-US)旗下雲端部門及微軟(MSFT-US)合作，協助兩家公司開發客製化AI晶片。邁威爾8月與Alphabet(GOOGL-US)旗下Google達成晶片協議，支援Google自行開發的AI晶片張量處理器(TPU)，協議也讓Google有權購買價值最高122億美元的邁威爾股票。
隨著客製化AI晶片及網路產品需求激增，邁威爾已成為AI支出熱潮的最大受惠者之一，今年股價幾乎上漲兩倍。邁威爾本月稍早將2028會計年度營收預測從150億美元上修至200億美元，理由是資料中心使用的客製化AI晶片及網路產品需求強勁。
不過Bernstein分析師表示，這筆潛在交易的規模可能引發市場對融資及整合問題的疑慮，並指出以如此龐大的收購規模，邁威爾可能無法完全以現金支付收購款項。截至最近一季，邁威爾的現金及約當現金約為39.2億美元。
paras_en: As the artificial‑intelligence (AI) industry races to scale up, Bloomberg reported, citing sources, that Marvell Technology (MRVL‑US) is in deep talks with data‑center optics maker Lumen­tium (LITE‑US) about a possible acquisition to simplify its supply chain.

Both companies, headquartered in Northern California, have opened negotiations, underscoring how AI development is sparking a merger frenzy that investors view as having massive growth potential. Lumen­tium’s market value is currently about $83 billion, while Marvell’s is roughly $221 billion.

Sources say the deal could be announced as early as next week, but because no final agreement has been reached, the talks could still fall apart and timing details may change. Neither Marvell nor Lumen­tium commented on the matter.

After the acquisition rumor broke, Marvell’s after‑hours share price fell about 9% on Wednesday, while Lumen­tium’s surged roughly 11%, lifting its market cap to about $91 billion. Lumen­tium’s stock is up 148% year‑to‑date, closing at $913.95 per share on Wednesday’s regular session.
Bloomberg’s data indicate that if the transaction closes, it could squeeze into the top ten largest mergers ever in the technology and telecommunications sectors.

Lumen­tium manufactures lasers and other optical‑technology products used for high‑speed, high‑volume data transmission. Such hardware is a key foundation of the AI boom, enabling data‑centers and telecom operators to move information between servers, facilities and other destinations.

Marvell, a semiconductor maker, currently buys laser products from Lumen­tium, so the deal could streamline its supply chain. Marvell is ramping up its optics and photonics capabilities to connect data‑center equipment and earlier this year acquired photonics firm Celestial AI.

Nvidia (NVDA‑US) previously invested $2 billion in Lumen­tium, with an agreement that the two would cooperate on photonics technology. Photonics uses light rather than traditional copper wiring to transmit data, allowing faster and more efficient information transfer.

Marvell also works with Amazon’s (AMZN‑US) cloud division and Microsoft (MSFT‑US) to help the two firms develop custom AI chips. In August, Marvell struck a chip deal with Google, an Alphabet (GOOGL‑US) subsidiary, to support Google’s own AI tensor‑processing units (TPUs) and gave Google the right to purchase up to $12.2 billion of Marvell stock.

With exploding demand for custom AI chips and networking gear, Marvell has become one of the biggest beneficiaries of the AI‑spending surge, its stock having nearly doubled this year. Earlier this month Marvell lifted its FY 2028 revenue outlook from $15 billion to $20 billion, citing strong demand for custom AI chips and networking products in data centers.

However, Bernstein analysts warn that the sheer size of the potential deal could raise market concerns about financing and integration, noting that a transaction of this magnitude may not be payable entirely in cash. As of the most recent quarter, Marvell’s cash and cash equivalents were about $3.92 billion.

paras_en: On October 29, 2026 (U-Analysis/Industry Data Center report) – Microsoft (MSFT-US) saw its cloud business accelerate, temporarily easing market concerns about the payback of massive AI investments. The company announced on the 28th that for the first quarter of its fiscal 2027 year ending September, both revenue and profit beat expectations, and free cash flow reached $18.6 billion, more than double market estimates. Microsoft also expects Azure growth to speed up further this quarter, driving the stock up more than 5% in after‑hours trading.

Microsoft’s first‑quarter revenue rose 20% year‑over‑year to $92.28 billion; adjusted earnings per share were $4.89, above the market forecast of $4.73. Azure revenue grew 48% year‑over‑year to $33.17 billion, beating the estimate of $32.84 billion. This is the first time the market can directly compare Azure’s quarterly revenue with that of other major cloud providers since Microsoft began disclosing the figure.

Looking ahead to the second quarter ending December, Microsoft expects Azure revenue to grow 49%‑50%, higher than the market’s 47.6% estimate. Overall revenue is projected between $96.0 billion and $97.1 billion, also topping the market’s $95.6 billion outlook, indicating continued strong demand for cloud and AI services from enterprises.

CEO Satya Nadella told analysts that the AI market is shifting from a chase for new technology to longer‑term enterprise deployments. Customers are no longer just a handful of large players buying compute power each quarter; increasingly, firms are planning investments for the next ten years or more. For Microsoft, expanding the customer base helps reduce the risk of relying on a few big clients for cloud growth.

However, the free cash flow surge this quarter was partly due to delayed capital expenditures. Microsoft’s Q1 capex was $45.2 billion, up from $34.9 billion a year earlier but still below the company’s original $50 billion target; free cash flow hit $18.6 billion, well above the market’s $8.54 billion estimate.

Investor Relations Vice President Jonathan Neilson explained that some third‑party capacity originally scheduled for Q1 delivery was postponed, resulting in lower spending than expected, not a change in the investment plan. Microsoft’s cumulative capex for the first three quarters this year reached $118.1 billion; to meet the $175 billion full‑year target set in July, another $56.9 billion will be needed in Q4.

This means Microsoft’s cash‑flow performance was impressive this quarter, but spending pressure remains. As the delayed capacity comes online, whether Azure can keep accelerating growth to support the massive infrastructure outlay will be a key focus for the market going forward.

paras: 2026年10月29日（優分析／產業數據中心報導）⸺ Google母公司Alphabet(GOOGL-US)雲端業務成長強勁，卻抵不過廣告收入不如預期與AI投資支出攀升。公司28日公布第三季營收、獲利均低於市場預估，自由現金流連續第二季為負，缺口擴大至90.7億美元，帶動股價盤後重挫逾10%。
Alphabet第三季營收達1,276億美元，低於市場預期的1,282億美元；歸屬普通股股東淨利年減25%，降至261.7億美元，調整後每股盈餘為2.67美元，也不及市場預估的3.02美元。主要落差來自核心廣告業務，當季廣告收入為820.1億美元，比市場預期少約14.1億美元。
相較之下，Google Cloud第三季營收較去年同期增加逾一倍，達307.1億美元，優於市場預期，成為財報中的亮點。雲端執行長Thomas Kurian首次出席財報電話會議，並表示自研張量處理器(TPU)的銷售，已對雲端業務帶來可觀貢獻。
Google正透過跨年度雲端與AI基礎建設合約，擴大資安、零售及金融服務等企業客戶。除了採購輝達NVIDIA(NVDA-US)的GPU，自研TPU也成為擴充算力供給的重要工具。不過，雲端業務快速成長，仍未能彌補廣告收入的落差。
市場更在意的是，AI投入持續侵蝕現金流。Alphabet第二季自由現金流為負59億美元，是上市22年來首度轉負，第三季缺口進一步擴大至90.7億美元，明顯遜於市場原先預期的接近損益兩平。除了擴充雲端產能，公司也持續投入AI研發；主要反映相關研發費用的「Alphabet層級活動」，當季營業虧損達76.6億美元。
財務長Anat Ashkenazi表示，今年資本支出預估維持不變，但2027年將顯著增加。她也預期，使用第三方雲端產能，短期內將對利潤率造成壓力，意味即使營收持續擴大，成本負擔仍難立即減輕。
Alphabet同日推出Gemini 4 Carbon新模型，執行長皮查在法說會上強調，公司已重新站上AI技術前沿。不過，從財報公布後的股價反應來看，投資人除了關注模型進展，也愈來愈要求AI成長能轉化為獲利與現金流。

paras_en: October 29, 2026 (U-Analysis/Industry Data Center report) – Alphabet (GOOGL-US), Google’s parent company, saw strong growth in its cloud business, but it could not offset weaker‑than‑expected ad revenue and rising AI investment costs. The company reported third‑quarter revenue and profit below market forecasts on the 28th, with free cash flow turning negative for the second consecutive quarter, widening the shortfall to $9.07 billion and sending the stock down more than 10% in after‑hours trading.

Alphabet’s third‑quarter revenue reached $127.6 billion, missing the market estimate of $128.2 billion. Net income attributable to common shareholders fell 25% year‑over‑year to $26.17 billion, and adjusted earnings per share came in at $2.67, below the consensus forecast of $3.02. The main shortfall stemmed from core advertising, with ad revenue for the quarter at $82.01 billion, about $1.41 billion less than analysts had expected.

In contrast, Google Cloud’s third‑quarter revenue more than doubled year‑over‑year to $30.71 billion, beating expectations and emerging as the bright spot in the earnings release. Cloud CEO Thomas Kurian appeared at the earnings call for the first time and said sales of its in‑house Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) have made a sizable contribution to the cloud business.

Google is expanding enterprise contracts for cloud and AI infrastructure across sectors such as cybersecurity, retail and financial services. In addition to purchasing NVIDIA (NVDA‑US) GPUs, its self‑developed TPUs have become a key tool for scaling compute capacity. Nevertheless, the rapid growth of the cloud segment still falls short of offsetting the advertising revenue gap.

The market’s bigger concern is that AI spending continues to erode cash flow. Alphabet posted a negative free cash flow of $5.9 billion in the second quarter – the first quarterly deficit in its 22‑year public history – and the shortfall widened to $9.07 billion in the third quarter, well below analysts’ expectations of near‑breakeven cash flow. While the company is expanding cloud capacity, it is also persisting with AI R&D; the “Alphabet‑level activities” that capture related R&D expenses recorded an operating loss of $7.66 billion for the quarter.

Chief Financial Officer Anat Ashkenazi said capital expenditures are expected to stay flat this year but will rise sharply in 2027. She also warned that relying on third‑party cloud capacity will put short‑term pressure on profit margins, meaning that even as revenue grows, cost burdens will not ease immediately.

Alphabet unveiled the Gemini 4 Carbon model on the same day, and CEO Pichai emphasized at the earnings call that the company has reclaimed its position at the forefront of AI technology. However, the post‑earnings stock reaction shows investors are not only watching model progress but are increasingly demanding that AI growth translate into profits and cash flow.
